subjects.name: Fundamentals of Information Technology
subjects.description: Computer components and history, hardware and storage, software and databases, networks and the internet, and emerging IT trends.
keyUnits: Basic Computer Organization and Computer Peripherals

subjects.name: Mathematics-I
subjects.description: Matrix algebra, coordinate systems and geometry, vectors and solid geometry, and applications of differentiation.

subjects.name: Technical Communication
subjects.description: Oral presentation skills, intensive and extensive reading, and professional business/technical writing.

subjects.name: Society and Ethics in IT
subjects.description: Sociology fundamentals, social and cultural change, Nepali society, professional ethics in IT, and emotional intelligence.
keyUnits: Historical Characteristics of Nepali Society and Culture

subjects.name: Computer Programming in C
subjects.description: Procedural programming fundamentals in C — control flow, arrays, functions, pointers, structures, and file handling.
keyUnits: Files and File Handling in C

subjects.name: Project-I
subjects.description: Group software project (2-3 students) built in C, covering requirement gathering through implementation and oral defense — 45 lab hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics-II
subjects.description: Multiple integrals, differential equations, Fourier series, and functions of a complex variable.
keyUnits: Differential Equations of the First Order

subjects.name: Digital Logic
subjects.description: Number systems, Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuit design, registers and counters.

subjects.name: Discrete Structure
subjects.description: Set theory, counting, logic, relations, graphs and trees, order relations, and automata theory.

subjects.name: Object-Oriented Programming in C++
subjects.description: C++ OOP fundamentals — classes, constructors, operator overloading, inheritance, polymorphism, templates, and file handling.

subjects.name: Financial Management and Accounting
subjects.description: Financial management fundamentals, capital budgeting and structure, and core accounting processes and statements.

subjects.name: Project-II
subjects.description: Group software project (2-3 students) built using Object-Oriented Programming in C++ — 45 lab hours.

subjects.name: Numerical Methods
subjects.description: Numerical solutions to nonlinear equations, interpolation, linear systems, differentiation/integration, and ODEs.
keyUnits: System of Linear Equations (Direct & Indirect Methods)

subjects.name: Microcontroller
subjects.description: 8051 microcontroller architecture, instruction set, I/O and timer programming, interrupts, and peripheral interfacing.

subjects.name: Data Structure and Algorithm
subjects.description: Core data structures — stacks, queues, lists, trees, graphs — plus sorting, searching, and algorithm efficiency.

subjects.name: Computer Network and Data Communication
subjects.description: Networking fundamentals, the OSI/TCP-IP layered model, data link/network/transport layers, and network security.

subjects.name: System Analysis and Design
subjects.description: SDLC models, process/conceptual modeling with DFDs and ERDs, systems analysis and design, and object-oriented analysis with UML.
keyUnits: Overview of Systems Analysis & Design (SDLC Models)

subjects.name: Project-III
subjects.description: Group project (2-3 students) developing a microcontroller (BIT202CO)-based system — 45 lab hours.

subjects.name: Probability and Statistics
subjects.description: Descriptive statistics, probability theory, theoretical distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, and correlation/regression.
keyUnits: Estimation theory and testing of hypothesis

subjects.name: Computer Organization and Architecture
subjects.description: Computer instruction sets, control unit design, CPU architecture, pipelining, memory organization, and multiprocessors.

subjects.name: Operating System
subjects.description: Process/thread management, memory management, file systems, I/O, deadlocks, and distributed systems.

subjects.name: Database Management System
subjects.description: DBMS architecture, relational model, SQL, normalization, database security, and transaction/query processing.
keyUnits: Database System Concepts and Architecture (E-R model)
Transaction and Query Processing (ACID, concurrency, WAL)

subjects.name: Programming in JAVA
subjects.description: Core Java OOP, GUI programming, file I/O, JDBC, socket programming, and Servlet/JSP.

subjects.name: Project-IV
subjects.description: Group application software project (up to 3 students) developed in Java, with proposal, mid-term, and final presentation.

subjects.name: Research Methodology
subjects.description: Scientific inquiry, quantitative and qualitative research designs, hypothesis formulation, and technical writing.

subjects.name: Computer Graphics
subjects.description: Rasterization algorithms, 2D/3D transformations, clipping, illumination, and shading.

subjects.name: Cryptography and Network Security
subjects.description: Classical and modern ciphers, public key cryptosystems, digital signatures, hash functions, and network security protocols.

subjects.name: Web Technology
subjects.description: Web technology fundamentals. Unit contents pending the official Semester V syllabus PDF — the previous entry described a React/Next.js course that is not the PU syllabus.

subjects.name: Internet of Things
subjects.description: IoT fundamentals. Unit contents pending the official Semester V syllabus PDF; this subject was missing from the data entirely.

subjects.name: Project-V
subjects.description: Group project carrying the semester's practical assessment. Evaluation criteria pending the official Semester V syllabus PDF.

subjects.name: Artificial Intelligence
subjects.description: AI foundations from agents and search through knowledge representation, learning, reasoning, expert systems, neural networks, and NLP.
keyUnits: Uninformed & Informed Search (BFS, DFS, A*, Hill Climbing)
Adversarial Search & Constraint Satisfaction (Minimax, Alpha-Beta, CSP)

subjects.name: Management Information System (MIS)
subjects.description: Information systems in global business, IT infrastructure, decision support and executive systems, and the strategic/security role of MIS.
keyUnits: Information Systems in Global Business Today
Decision Support Systems (DSS) & Executive Information Systems (EIS)

subjects.name: Data Warehousing and Mining
subjects.description: Data warehouse architecture and OLAP, plus core data mining techniques — association rule mining, classification, and cluster analysis.
keyUnits: Introduction to Data Mining & Data Warehousing
Mining Association Rules (Apriori, Market Basket Analysis)

subjects.name: Simulation and Modeling
subjects.description: Simulation concepts and system types, the Monte Carlo method, random number generation and randomness testing, and analyzing simulation output.
keyUnits: Simulation of Continuous Systems (Queuing, Markov Chains)
Random Numbers: Generation & Testing (Chi-Square, Poker Test)
Analysis of Simulation Output & Replication of Runs

subjects.name: Software Engineering
subjects.description: The software engineering lifecycle — process models, project management, requirements, design, testing, and quality metrics.
keyUnits: Process Models (Waterfall, Prototyping, RAD, Spiral, Agile)
Software Project Management (4Ps, COCOMO, Risk, Scheduling)
SE Trends: Agile, XP, Cloud Computing, SOA

subjects.name: Project-VI
subjects.description: Group web-based application project (up to 3 students) built with server-side scripting, on a topic related to Artificial Intelligence or Data Mining — 45 lab hours, evaluated across title, mid-term, and pre-final presentations.
keyUnits: AI or Data Mining-Related Project Topic

subjects.name: Network Programming
subjects.description: Client-server socket programming — TCP/UDP sockets, I/O multiplexing, broadcast/multicast, and raw sockets in C/Unix.
keyUnits: Elementary Socket Calls (socket, bind, connect, accept)

subjects.name: Digital Governance
subjects.description: e-Government implementation and policy, ICT infrastructure, security, digital democracy, and case studies including Nepal's GIDC.

subjects.name: Specialization Track (2 of 4 courses)
subjects.description: Choose one specialization track and take 2 courses in Sem 7, 2 more in Sem 8: (A) Intelligent Systems & Business Analytics — Machine Learning, Business Intelligence & Data Science, Deep Learning; (B) Digital Commerce & Mobile App Development — Digital Commerce, Multimedia & Application; (C) Climate Change Management — GIS, Remote Sensing, Data Center & Disaster Recovery.
keyUnits: Track A: Business Intelligence & Data Science (BIT422CO)

subjects.name: Internship
subjects.description: 45-hour supervised internship at a partner organization (bank, hospital, software company, telecom, or government IT unit), evaluated via proposal defense, mid-term, and end-term report.

subjects.name: Principles of Management and Entrepreneurship in IT
subjects.description: Management fundamentals, organization design, entrepreneurship, business planning, and IT product marketing/technology transfer.

subjects.name: Distributed and Cloud Computing
subjects.description: Distributed systems fundamentals and cloud computing service/deployment models, virtualization, and cloud security.

subjects.name: Specialization Track (2 of 4 courses, continued)
subjects.description: Second half of the Sem 7 specialization track: (A) Intelligent Systems & Business Analytics — Natural Language Processing, Supply Chain Analytics; (B) Digital Commerce & Mobile App Development — Big Data, Mobile App Development; (C) Climate Change Management — Incident Response, Climate Change Risk Management, Disaster Governance.
keyUnits: Track C: Climate Change Risk Management (BIT486CO)

subjects.name: Apprentice Project
subjects.description: 45-hour capstone project developing a 2-tier/3-tier/n-tier application with client-side and server-side scripting on any RDBMS.
